title: Non-Idempotent Network Retry
pattern: A mutating state request (POST/PUT/PATCH) retried across the network without a unique transaction/idempotency key passed to the server.
why_bad: If the initial request succeeded but the response (ACK) got lost due to a network glitch, retrying the bare request causes the server to perform the action multiple times (e.g., charging a customer twice) [23:171].
detection: Outbound write requests wrapped in a retry block that do not generate, carry, or propagate a unique UUID or token across retries [39:53].
fix: Generate a persistent request identifier (Idempotency Key) on the client, propagate it on every retry, and verify it on the server using a deduplication cache [39:53].
